import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The Andrews-Curtis conjecture

The conjecture says that every normally generating `n`-tuple in the free group
on `n` generators is Andrews-Curtis equivalent to the standard free basis.

References:

* [Wikipedia, Andrews-Curtis conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrews%E2%80%93Curtis_conjecture)
* [A. D. Myasnikov, A. G. Myasnikov and V. Shpilrain,
  *On the Andrews-Curtis equivalence*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0302080)
-/

namespace AndrewsCurtis

/-- An `n`-tuple of relators in the free group on `n` generators. -/
abbrev RelatorTuple (n : ℕ) := Fin n → FreeGroup (Fin n)

/-- The standard relator tuple, consisting of the free generators themselves. -/
def standardRelators (n : ℕ) : RelatorTuple n :=
  fun i ↦ FreeGroup.of i

/--
The elementary Andrews-Curtis moves: inversion or multiplication of relators,
interchange of two relators, and conjugation of one relator by an arbitrary word.
-/
inductive Move {n : ℕ} : RelatorTuple n → RelatorTuple n → Prop
  | invert (r : RelatorTuple n) (i : Fin n) :
      Move r (Function.update r i (r i)⁻¹)
  | multiply (r : RelatorTuple n) (i j : Fin n) (hij : i ≠ j) :
      Move r (Function.update r i (r i * r j))
  | swap (r : RelatorTuple n) (i j : Fin n) :
      Move r (fun k ↦ r (Equiv.swap i j k))
  | conjugate (r : RelatorTuple n) (i : Fin n) (w : FreeGroup (Fin n)) :
      Move r (Function.update r i (w * r i * w⁻¹))

/-- Andrews-Curtis equivalence is the equivalence relation generated by elementary moves. -/
def Equivalent {n : ℕ} : RelatorTuple n → RelatorTuple n → Prop :=
  Relation.EqvGen Move

/--
A relator tuple normally generates the free group when the normal closure of its
range is the whole free group. Equivalently, the associated balanced presentation
presents the trivial group.
-/
def NormallyGenerates {n : ℕ} (r : RelatorTuple n) : Prop :=
  Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range r) = ⊤

/--
**The Andrews-Curtis conjecture.**

Every normally generating `n`-tuple in the free group of rank `n` is
Andrews-Curtis equivalent to the standard tuple of free generators.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem andrews_curtis_conjecture (n : ℕ) (r : RelatorTuple n)
    (hr : NormallyGenerates r) :
    Equivalent r (standardRelators n) := by
  sorry

end AndrewsCurtis

reformulations.difference: Lean uses the equivalence closure of four move types, including swaps. The cited paper defines equivalence by finite sequences of AC1–AC3, without listing swaps separately.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Swaps are redundant: on two coordinates, (a,b) → (a,b⁻¹) → (ab⁻¹,b⁻¹) → (ba⁻¹,b⁻¹) → (ba⁻¹,a⁻¹) → (ba⁻¹,a) → (b,a), using only inversion and right multiplication. Swapping an index with itself is the identity. Every basic move also has a finite forward inverse: inversion is self-inverse, conjugation is reversed by the inverse conjugator, and multiplication is reversed by inverting the other coordinate, multiplying, and restoring that coordinate. Consequently equivalence closure is exactly finite AC1–AC3 reachability. Proved as Review.equivalent_iff_path in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The paper states a biconditional for rank n ≥ 2; Lean states the normally-generating-to-equivalent implication for every natural-number rank.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The omitted implication is unconditional: all moves preserve normal closure, and the standard free generators normally generate the free group. The additional ranks are harmless. At rank 0 the unique empty tuple is equivalent to itself and the free group is trivial. At rank 1, normal generation holds exactly when the sole relator is the generator or its inverse, so at most one inversion suffices. Combining these facts with the move-relation equivalence gives precisely the paper's statement. The complete equivalence is proved as Review.full_iff_source_statement.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0302080 — Myasnikov, Myasnikov and Shpilrain, On the Andrews-Curtis equivalence, especially §1 (AC1–AC3, the conjecture, and the separate stabilized variant).
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_transformation — Definitions, including the decomposition of a swap into inversions and multiplications.
review.notes: All declarations were checked. The fixed-rank formulation faithfully states the conjecture, not its weaker stabilized variant. The research open tag agrees with the consulted Wikipedia article. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully and proves the reformulations, the normal-closure/trivial-quotient characterization, and the low-rank cases; axiom checks show no sorryAx dependencies. Rank-2 evaluations also confirm the intended effects of all four move constructors.
